text:
james: opened a PR to update the Dedicated autoscale docs + migration guide. changes: autoscale schema v2, cooldown default moved 60->120s, label normalization, and new SDK examples. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6790

nina: quick read. why bump cooldown to 120s? worried about impact on request-level latency during sudden spikes. do we have perf numbers? :thinking_face:

james: short note in the PR description with a small perf run + numbers. TL;DR: 30% fewer scale churn events in our synthetic spike test (1k rps -> 10k rps) but median latency for bursty single requests increased ~15ms. graphs TODO.

tom: can we include concrete SDK snippets for ops teams to set cooldown and scale_policy programmatically? i'll add a Go sample and a Python sample inline. here's the python one to start:

```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
policy = {
  "name": "default-autoscale",
  "cooldown_seconds": 120,
  "scale_up": {"step": 2, "max_per_min": 10},
  "scale_down": {"step": 1, "stabilization_seconds": 300}
}
client.update_autoscale_policy("reservation-123", policy)
```

ryan: ops wants a CLI detect + remediation example to find reservations using old label key `owner`. suggest: 

```bash
# find reservations with owner label
redwood-cli reservations list --format json \
  | jq '.[] | select(.labels.owner != null) | {id: .id, labels: .labels}'
# quick migration (dry-run, then remove --apply)
redwood-cli reservations list --format json \
  | jq -r '.[] | select(.labels.owner != null) | @base64' \
  | while read r; do echo $r | base64 --decode | jq -r '.id'; done
```

nina: thanks. also please reword the SLA reroute paragraph — legal prefers explicit language. propose: "If Dedicated capacity is unavailable, Redwood may route requests to compatible hosted model variants. Such reroutes are not covered by the Dedicated SLA unless the customer contract explicitly states otherwise. Customers will receive alerts in the Console and via configured webhooks when automatic reroutes occur."

james: updated the PR with that wording and added a short migration checklist section (preflight jq queries, backup labels, run remap). left a TODO for perf graphs.

tom: small nit on naming: the docs currently call the field `preemption_policy: best-effort`. infra renamed it to `preemption_policy: allow-preempt` in the new API. can you align examples?

james: fixed examples to `allow-preempt` and added a Go SDK snippet per Tom's earlier note. Go snippet pasted in the PR.

ryan: LGTM for ops. one more thing — add a short note in release notes about the cooldown default change and the recommended steps for high-burst workloads (reduce cooldown on a per-reservation basis if needed).
